payment_diversion.title: Possible payment diversion
payment_diversion.summary: Money may have been paid to a criminal after banking details changed. Act on step one now.

steps.title: Call your bank's fraud line now
steps.why: Only your bank can try to stop or recall the payment. Minutes count.
do: Choose your bank and call its official fraud line.
Say: I made a payment to a fraudulent account. Please try to stop or recall it.
Write down the reference number.

steps.title: Confirm with your supplier on a number you already had
steps.why: Do not reply to the suspicious email or call a number in it.
do: Use a number from an old invoice, your contacts or the supplier's official website.
Ask if they genuinely changed their banking details.

steps.title: Check your mailbox
steps.why: Criminals may hide or forward messages so they can watch payment conversations.
do: Look for forwarding and inbox rules you did not create.
Check recent sign-ins and change your password from a clean device.
Turn on two-step verification.

steps.title: Keep the evidence
steps.why: Your bank, SAPS and insurer may ask for the message and proof of payment.
do: Do not delete the email or message.
Save the proof of payment and screenshots.
The evidence pack feature is next in this build.

mailbox_compromise.title: Possible hacked mailbox
mailbox_compromise.summary: Lock the mailbox before it is used to send fraudulent invoices.

steps.title: Lock the account
do: Change the password from a clean device.
Turn on two-step verification and sign out other sessions.

steps.title: Remove unknown rules
steps.why: Forwarding rules can keep leaking email after a password change.
do: Remove rules and forwarding you did not create.
Keep screenshots for IT support.

suspicious_message.title: Suspicious message — no money moved
suspicious_message.summary: Good: you may be able to stop the scam before money leaves.

steps.title: Don't pay, click or reply
steps.why: A changed-bank-details message is a common payment-diversion tactic.
do: Do not change any banking details from the message.
Confirm the request on a trusted number.

not_cyber.title: This may not be a cyber incident
not_cyber.summary: It sounds like a normal payment or admin problem, but stay cautious.

steps.title: Double-check before you relax
steps.why: Scams can look like an ordinary late payment.
do: If details changed, start again and treat it as suspicious.
If money left for an unfamiliar account, call your bank.

unsure.title: Let's be safe
unsure.summary: We could not tell what happened. Start with the safest action if money moved.

steps.title: If money moved, call your bank now
steps.why: The bank may be able to stop the payment.
do: Choose your bank below and call its official fraud number.
